```{r}
if(!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("tximport", "DESeq2", "org.Mm.eg.db"))
```

```{r}

library(tximport)
library(DESeq2)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(ggplot2)
library(pheatmap)
library(ggrepel)
```

```{r}
#==============================================================================
# 1. IMPORT SALMON DATA
#==============================================================================

# Read samples
samples <- read.csv("//wsl.localhost/Ubuntu/home/maha/rnaseq_trm/metadata/samples_file.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
files <- file.path("//wsl.localhost/Ubuntu/home/maha/rnaseq_trm/salmon", samples$sample, "quant.sf")
names(files) <- samples$sample
all(file.exists(files))

# Read one file to build tx2gene mapping
test <- read.delim(files[1])
head(test)

# Create tx2gene from the pipe-delimited transcript info
tx2gene <- data.frame(
  TXNAME = as.character(test$Name),
  GENEID = sapply(strsplit(as.character(test$Name), "\\|"), function(x) {
    gene <- x[2]  # Second field is gene ID
    sub("\\..*", "", gene)  # Remove version number (.1, .2, etc.)
  }),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
head(tx2gene, 20)
dim(tx2gene)

# Import salmon quantification data and summarize to gene level
txi <- tximport(
  files,
  type = "salmon",
  tx2gene = tx2gene,
  dropInfReps = TRUE
)

# Check the tximport objects
str(txi)
names(txi)
dim(txi$counts)
dim(txi$abundance)
dim(txi$length)
head(txi$counts)
head(txi$abundance)
```

```{r}
#==============================================================================
# 2. CREATE DESEQ2 OBJECT
#==============================================================================

# Make sure condition is a factor
samples$condition <- factor(samples$condition)

# Check samples match
all(colnames(txi$counts) == samples$sample)

# Create DESeq2 object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromTximport(
  txi,
  colData = samples,
  design = ~ condition
)

# Add Gene symbols to dds object 
# Get ensembl IDs from dds rownames
ensembl_ids <- rownames(dds)

# Map to gene symbols
gene_symbols <- mapIds(
  org.Mm.eg.db,
  keys = ensembl_ids,
  column = "SYMBOL",
  keytype = "ENSEMBL",
  multiVals = "first"
)

# Add as a new column in rowData
mcols(dds)$symbol <- gene_symbols

# For genes without symbols, use Ensembl ID
mcols(dds)$symbol[is.na(mcols(dds)$symbol)] <- ensembl_ids[is.na(mcols(dds)$symbol)]
head(mcols(dds))

# Pre-filtering: remove genes with very low counts
# Keeping genes with atleast 10 reads total across all samples
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds)) >= 10
dds <- dds[keep,]

# Run DESeq2
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# Check how many genes remain
nrow(dds)
```

```{r}
#==============================================================================
# 3. DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION ANALYSIS
#==============================================================================

# Moving forward with analysis, there are 3 major conditions as we know or 3 different cell types the CD103+, CD49+, CD103-49-
# Here, CD103+ is stem like TRM cells, which is promoted by TGF-Beta, non-attacking but is involved in long term immunity
# CD49+ is another TRM cells, which is nothing but differentiated CD103+ after vaccination, promoted by IL-2, which attacks the cancerous cells.
# CD103-49- are non-resident TRM cells, which don't create an impact.
# So, I am going to consider the CD103-49- as the reference and compare the other 2 to it. Also compare the CD49+ to CD103+ to understand what differential gene expression changes after vaccination

head(samples$condition)

# Get comparisons
res_CD103_vs_DN <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "CD103+", "CD103-CD49-"))
res_CD49_vs_DN <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "CD49+", "CD103-CD49-"))
res_stemlike_vs_effector <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "CD103+", "CD49+"))

# Summary of results
summary(res_CD103_vs_DN)
summary(res_CD49_vs_DN)
summary(res_stemlike_vs_effector)

# Based on the summary, we could see many genes are differential expressed between CD103_vs_DN and stemlike_vs_effector
# Whereas the comparison between CD49_vs_DN have very few DEGs

# Add gene symbols to results dataframes
res_CD103_vs_DN_df <- as.data.frame(res_CD103_vs_DN)
res_CD103_vs_DN_df$ensembl <- rownames(res_CD103_vs_DN_df)
res_CD103_vs_DN_df$symbol <- mcols(dds)[rownames(res_CD103_vs_DN_df), "symbol"]

res_CD49_vs_DN_df <- as.data.frame(res_CD49_vs_DN)
res_CD49_vs_DN_df$ensembl <- rownames(res_CD49_vs_DN_df)
res_CD49_vs_DN_df$symbol <- mcols(dds)[rownames(res_CD49_vs_DN_df), "symbol"]

res_stemlike_vs_effector_df <- as.data.frame(res_stemlike_vs_effector)
res_stemlike_vs_effector_df$ensembl <- rownames(res_stemlike_vs_effector_df)
res_stemlike_vs_effector_df$symbol <- mcols(dds)[rownames(res_stemlike_vs_effector_df), "symbol"]

# Save results with gene symbols
write.csv(res_CD103_vs_DN_df[order(res_CD103_vs_DN_df$padj), ], 
          "results/CD103_stemlike_vs_DoublenegativeNonTRM.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(res_CD49_vs_DN_df[order(res_CD49_vs_DN_df$padj), ], 
          "results/CD49_effector_vs_DoublenegativeNonTRM.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(res_stemlike_vs_effector_df[order(res_stemlike_vs_effector_df$padj), ], 
          "results/CD103_STEMLIKE_vs_CD49_EFFECTOR.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#==============================================================================
# 4. VISUALIZATIONS
#==============================================================================

# Get variance stabilized data for plotting
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = FALSE)

#-------------------------------------
# PCA
#-------------------------------------
pcaData <- plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = "condition", returnData = TRUE)
percentVar <- round(100 * attr(pcaData, "percentVar"))

ggplot(pcaData, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = condition, label = name)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_text(vjust = -1, size = 3) +
  xlab(paste0("PC1: ", percentVar[1], "% variance")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2: ", percentVar[2], "% variance")) +
  ggtitle("PCA: Clustering cells based on condition and checking if DN cluster with CD49+?") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("CD103-CD49-" = "orange",
                                "CD49+" = "blue",
                                "CD103+" = "red"))
ggsave("results/PCA_check_DN_clustering.pdf", width = 10, height = 8)

# Yes, DN samples and CD49+ samples clusters together. 
# whereas, CD103+ samples are variable, there is 44% variance between CD49+ and DN samples.

#---------------------------------------------------
# MA plot
#---------------------------------------------------

# MA plot shows us how gene expression changes between 2 conditions,
# as a function of how highly expressed the gene is overall.
# M = Minus (log fold change), A = Average (mean expression)
# X = mean of normalized counts across all samples (left -> lowly expressed genes, right -> highly expressed genes)
# How much RNA is there overall?
# Y-axis: M (log2 fold change)
# y = log2(expression in cond A/ cond B)
# 0 - No change, +1 - 2*higher in cond A, -1 - 2*lower in cond A

pdf("results/MA_plot_CD103_vs_DN.pdf", width = 8, height = 6)
plotMA(res_CD103_vs_DN, ylim = c(-5, 5), 
       main = "CD103+ stem-like vs CD103-CD49- (Double Negative)")
abline(h = c(-1, 1), col = "red", lty = 2)
dev.off()

pdf("results/MA_plot_CD49_vs_DN.pdf", width = 8, height = 6)
plotMA(res_CD49_vs_DN, ylim = c(-5, 5), 
       main = "CD49+ effector-like vs CD103-CD49- (Double Negative)")
abline(h = c(-1, 1), col = "red", lty = 2)
dev.off()

pdf("results/MA_plot_CD103+_vs_CD49+.pdf", width = 8, height = 6)
plotMA(res_stemlike_vs_effector, ylim = c(-5, 5), 
       main = "CD103+ stem-like vs CD49+ effector-like")
abline(h = c(-1, 1), col = "red", lty = 2)
dev.off()

#-------------------------------------
# Volcano Plot - CD103+ vs DN
#-------------------------------------

# Add significance categories
res_CD103_vs_DN_df$diffexpressed <- "NO"
res_CD103_vs_DN_df$diffexpressed[res_CD103_vs_DN_df$log2FoldChange > 1 & res_CD103_vs_DN_df$padj < 0.05] <- "UP in CD103+"
res_CD103_vs_DN_df$diffexpressed[res_CD103_vs_DN_df$log2FoldChange < -1 & res_CD103_vs_DN_df$padj < 0.05] <- "DOWN in CD103+"

# Clean data for plotting
res_CD103_vs_DN_clean <- res_CD103_vs_DN_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(symbol))

# Select top genes to label
label_df_CD103 <- res_CD103_vs_DN_clean %>%
  filter(
    diffexpressed != "NO",
    abs(log2FoldChange) > 2,
    padj < 0.01
  ) %>%
  arrange(padj) %>%
  head(50)

# Volcano plot
ggplot(res_CD103_vs_DN_clean, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), color = diffexpressed)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = label_df_CD103,
    aes(label = symbol),
    size = 3,
    max.overlaps = 20
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("DOWN in CD103+" = "blue", "NO" = "grey", "UP in CD103+" = "red")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "CD103+ stem-like vs CD103-CD49- (DN)",
    x = "log2 Fold Change",
    y = "-log10(adjusted p-value)",
    color = "Differential Expression"
  ) +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 12))

ggsave("results/Volcano_CD103_vs_DN.pdf", width = 10, height = 8)
```

```{r}
#-------------------------------------------
# Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA)
#-------------------------------------------
# Install required packages
if(!requireNamespace("clusterProfiler", quietly = TRUE))
  BiocManager::install("clusterProfiler")
if(!requireNamespace("enrichplot", quietly = TRUE))
  BiocManager::install("enrichplot")
if(!requireNamespace("msigdbr", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("msigdbr")
if(!requireNamespace("fgsea", quietly = TRUE))
  BiocManager::install("fgsea")


library(clusterProfiler)
library(enrichplot)
library(msigdbr)
library(fgsea)

# Prepare ranked gene list for GSEA
# For GSEA, we need a ranked list of all genes (not just the significant ones)
# Rank by: sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue) to prioritize both batch effect size and significance
# To get the results for CD103+ vs CD49+
head(res_stemlike_vs_effector_clean)
res_gsea <- res_stemlike_vs_effector_clean


# Create ranking metric: sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue)
# This considers both batch effect size (log2FC) and significance (pvalue)
res_gsea$rank_metric <- sign(res_gsea$log2FoldChange) * (-log10(res_gsea$pvalue))

# Create a named vector of gene ranks (use ENSEMBL IDs)
gene_list <- res_gsea$rank_metric
names(gene_list) <- res_gsea$ensembl
head(res_gsea[,c("symbol", "log2FoldChange", "pvalue", "rank_metric")], 20)

# If a gene has a high log2FC (upregulated in CD103+) and low p-value (significant), it gets a high score
# If a gene has low log2FC (downregulated in CD103+/ upregulated in CD49+) and low p-value it gets a high negative score
# Genes with a high p-value (not significant gets scores near 0)

# Sort from most positive (upregulated in CD103+) to most negative (upregulated in CD49+)
gene_list <- sort(gene_list, decreasing = TRUE)

# Check the ranking
head(gene_list, 20)


cat("\n Total genes in ranked list:", length(gene_list), "\n")
cat("\n Top 10 genes (most upregulated in CD103+): \n")
head(gene_list, 10)

cat("\n Bottom 10 genes (most upregulated in CD49+): \n")
tail(gene_list, 20)

# Get the hallmark gene sets from MSigDB
# Download hallmark gene sets for mouse
available_collection <- msigdbr_collections()
View(available_collection)
msigdb_hallmark <- msigdbr(species = "Mus musculus", category = "H")
hallmark_list <- split(msigdb_hallmark$ensembl_gene, msigdb_hallmark$gs_name)
cat("Total rows:", nrow(msigdb_hallmark), "\n")
cat("Number of pathways:", length(hallmark_list), "\n")

# Show first few pathway names
cat("\nFirst 5 pathway names:\n")
print(head(names(hallmark_list), 5))

# The size of first pathway
cat("\nNumber of genes in first pathway (", names(hallmark_list)[1], "):\n")
cat(length(hallmark_list[[1]]), "genes\n")

# first few genes from first pathway
cat("\nFirst 10 genes in this pathway:\n")
print(head(hallmark_list[[1]], 10))

# Summary of pathway sizes
pathway_sizes <- sapply(hallmark_list, length)
cat("\n=== Pathway size summary ===\n")
cat("Min genes in a pathway:", min(pathway_sizes), "\n")
cat("Max genes in a pathway:", max(pathway_sizes), "\n")
cat("Mean genes per pathway:", round(mean(pathway_sizes), 1), "\n")
cat("Median genes per pathway:", median(pathway_sizes), "\n")

# GO Biological Process (needs subcategory)
misgdb_go_bp <- msigdbr(
  species = "Mus musculus",
  category = "C5",
  subcategory = "GO:BP"
)
nrow(misgdb_go_bp)
go_bp_list <- split(misgdb_go_bp$ensembl_gene, misgdb_go_bp$gs_name)

# KEGG Pathways (legacy version commonly used)
msigdb_kegg <- msigdbr(
  species = "Mus musculus",
  category = "C2",
  subcategory = "CP:KEGG_LEGACY"
)

nrow(msigdb_kegg)

kegg_list <- split(msigdb_kegg$ensembl_gene, msigdb_kegg$gs_name)

# Reactome Pathways
msigdb_reactome <- msigdbr(
  species = "Mus musculus",
  category = "C2",
  subcategory = "CP:REACTOME"
)

reactome_list <- split(msigdb_reactome$ensembl_gene, msigdb_reactome$gs_name)

# Immunologic signatures
msigdb_immune <- msigdbr(
  species = "Mus musculus",
  category = "C7",
  subcategory = "IMMUNESIGDB"
)

cat("Total Immune signature rows:", nrow(msigdb_immune), "\n")
cat("Number of Immune signatures:", length(unique(msigdb_immune$gs_name)), "\n")

immune_list <- split(msigdb_immune$ensembl_gene, msigdb_immune$gs_name)

# RUN GSEA ON ALL GENE SET COLLECTIONS
# 1. Hallmark
fgsea_hallmark <- fgsea(
  pathways = hallmark_list,
  stats = gene_list,
  minSize = 15,
  maxSize = 500,
  nperm = 10000
)

fgsea_hallmark <- fgsea_hallmark[order(fgsea_hallmark$pval), ]
cat("Significant Hallmark pathways (padj < 0.05):", 
  sum(fgsea_hallmark$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

head(fgsea_hallmark, 10)

# GO Biological Process
cat("\n=== Running GSEA on GO:BP ===\n")
fgsea_go_bp <- fgsea(
  pathways = go_bp_list,
  stats = gene_list,
  minSize = 15,
  maxSize = 500,
  nperm = 10000
)
fgsea_go_bp <- fgsea_go_bp[order(fgsea_go_bp$pval), ]

cat("Significant GO:BP pathways (padj < 0.05):", 
    sum(fgsea_go_bp$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

head(fgsea_go_bp, 10)

# KEGG
cat("\n=== Running GSEA on KEGG ===\n")
fgsea_kegg <- fgsea(
  pathways = kegg_list,
  stats = gene_list,
  minSize = 15,
  maxSize = 500,
  nperm = 10000
)
fgsea_kegg <- fgsea_kegg[order(fgsea_kegg$pval), ]

cat("Significant KEGG pathways (padj < 0.05):", 
    sum(fgsea_kegg$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

head(fgsea_kegg, 10)

# Immunologic signatures
cat("\n=== Running GSEA on Immunologic Signatures ===\n")
fgsea_immune <- fgsea(
  pathways = immune_list,
  stats = gene_list,
  minSize = 15,
  maxSize = 500,
  nperm = 10000
)
fgsea_immune <- fgsea_immune[order(fgsea_immune$pval), ]

cat("Significant Immune signatures (padj < 0.05):", 
    sum(fgsea_immune$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

head(fgsea_immune, 20)

#==============================================================================
# GSEA Summary
#==============================================================================

cat("\n=== GSEA SUMMARY: CD103+ stem-like vs CD49+ effector ===\n\n")

# Hallmark
cat("HALLMARK PATHWAYS:\n")
cat("  Significant (padj < 0.05):", sum(fgsea_hallmark$padj < 0.05), "\n")
cat("  Enriched in CD103+:", sum(fgsea_hallmark$padj < 0.05 & fgsea_hallmark$NES > 0), "\n")
cat("  Enriched in CD49+:", sum(fgsea_hallmark$padj < 0.05 & fgsea_hallmark$NES < 0), "\n\n")

cat("Top 5 in CD103+ stem-like:\n")

cat("\nTop 5 in CD49+ effector:\n")

# GO BP
cat("\n\nGO BIOLOGICAL PROCESS:\n")
cat("  Significant (padj < 0.05):", sum(fgsea_go_bp$padj < 0.05), "\n")
cat("  Enriched in CD103+:", sum(fgsea_go_bp$padj < 0.05 & fgsea_go_bp$NES > 0), "\n")
cat("  Enriched in CD49+:", sum(fgsea_go_bp$padj < 0.05 & fgsea_go_bp$NES < 0), "\n\n")

# KEGG

cat("Key KEGG pathways in CD103+:\n")

                      c("pathway", "NES", "padj")], 10))
```

```{r}
]

)
```

```{r}
#==============================================================================
# COMPARISON FIGURE: All Three Comparisons Side-by-Side
#==============================================================================

# First, run GSEA on CD49+ vs DN
res_CD49_vs_DN_df <- as.data.frame(res_CD49_vs_DN)
res_CD49_vs_DN_df$ensembl <- rownames(res_CD49_vs_DN_df)

res_for_gsea_cd49_dn <- res_CD49_vs_DN_df[
  !is.na(res_CD49_vs_DN_df$pvalue) & 
  !is.na(res_CD49_vs_DN_df$log2FoldChange), 
]

res_for_gsea_cd49_dn$rank_metric <- sign(res_for_gsea_cd49_dn$log2FoldChange) * 
  (-log10(res_for_gsea_cd49_dn$pvalue))

gene_list_cd49_dn <- res_for_gsea_cd49_dn$rank_metric
names(gene_list_cd49_dn) <- res_for_gsea_cd49_dn$ensembl
gene_list_cd49_dn <- sort(gene_list_cd49_dn, decreasing = TRUE)

# Run GSEA
fgsea_hallmark_cd49_dn <- fgsea(
  pathways = hallmark_list,
  stats = gene_list_cd49_dn,
  minSize = 15,
  maxSize = 500,
  nperm = 10000
)

fgsea_hallmark_cd49_dn <- fgsea_hallmark_cd49_dn[order(fgsea_hallmark_cd49_dn$pval), ]

cat("CD49+ vs DN: Significant pathways:", 
    sum(fgsea_hallmark_cd49_dn$padj < 0.05), "\n")

# Now create comparison with all three
cd103_vs_cd49_data <- fgsea_hallmark %>%
  filter(pathway %in% top_pathways) %>%
  select(pathway, NES) %>%
  rename(CD103_vs_CD49 = NES)

cd103_vs_dn_data <- fgsea_hallmark_cd103_dn %>%
  filter(pathway %in% top_pathways) %>%
  select(pathway, NES) %>%
  rename(CD103_vs_DN = NES)

cd49_vs_dn_data <- fgsea_hallmark_cd49_dn %>%
  filter(pathway %in% top_pathways) %>%
  select(pathway, NES) %>%
  rename(CD49_vs_DN = NES)

# Join all three
comparison_data_full <- cd103_vs_cd49_data %>%
  left_join(cd103_vs_dn_data, by = "pathway") %>%
  left_join(cd49_vs_dn_data, by = "pathway")

# Pivot
comparison_long_full <- comparison_data_full %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(CD103_vs_CD49, CD103_vs_DN, CD49_vs_DN),
    names_to = "comparison",
    values_to = "NES"
  )

# Clean names
comparison_long_full$pathway_clean <- gsub("HALLMARK_", "", comparison_long_full$pathway)
comparison_long_full$pathway_clean <- gsub("_", " ", comparison_long_full$pathway_clean)

comparison_long_full$comparison_clean <- case_when(
  grepl("CD103_vs_CD49", comparison_long_full$comparison) ~ "CD103+ vs CD49+",
  grepl("CD103_vs_DN", comparison_long_full$comparison) ~ "CD103+ vs DN",
  grepl("CD49_vs_DN", comparison_long_full$comparison) ~ "CD49+ vs DN",
  TRUE ~ comparison_long_full$comparison
)

# Plot with three comparisons
p_comparison_full <- ggplot(comparison_long_full, 
                            aes(x = reorder(pathway_clean, NES), 
                                y = NES, 
                                fill = comparison_clean)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.85), width = 0.8) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "CD103+ vs CD49+" = "#E41A1C", 
      "CD103+ vs DN" = "#377EB8",
      "CD49+ vs DN" = "#4DAF4A"  # Green for the third comparison
    ),
    name = "Comparison"
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black", size = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Hallmark Pathways: All Pairwise Comparisons",
    subtitle = "CD49+ vs DN shows minimal differences (confirming similarity)",
    x = "",
    y = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray40"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(p_comparison_full)
ggsave("results/GSEA_comparison_all_three.pdf", p_comparison_full, width = 13, height = 9)
View(comparison_data_full)
```

```{r}
#==============================================================================
# Correlation Plot
#==============================================================================

library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
# Create scatter plot
p_correlation <- ggplot(comparison_data_full, 
                        aes(x = CD103_vs_CD49, 
                            y = CD103_vs_DN,
                            label = gsub("HALLMARK_", "", gsub("_", " ", pathway)))) +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.7, color = "red") +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_text_repel(size = 3, max.overlaps = 15) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black", alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = "CD49+ and DN Show Similar Enrichment Patterns",
    subtitle = "Points near diagonal line indicate similar NES in both comparisons\n(high correlation confirms CD49+ ≈ DN transcriptionally)",
    x = "NES: CD103+ vs CD49+",
    y = "NES: CD103+ vs DN"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray40")
  )

print(p_correlation)

# Calculate correlation
cor_value <- cor(comparison_data_full$CD103_vs_CD49, comparison_data_full$CD103_vs_DN)
cat("\nCorrelation between CD103+ vs CD49+ and CD103+ vs DN:", round(cor_value, 3), "\n")
cat("(High correlation confirms CD49+ and DN are transcriptionally similar)\n")
```
